thread:
alex_chang: quick heads-up — autotuner picks for quant kernels are causing odd latency cliffs around certain seqlen ranges, noticed on sm83 and sm86 nodes

maria_liu: which quant modes? int8/int4/fp8?

alex_chang: mainly INT4 and FP8 combos. INT8 generally stable, but INT4 gets chosen aggressively for short seqs and then we see a 8-12% latency regression at the seqlen->batch boundary (e.g., 480->512)

samir: can you paste the autotune output? also are KV cache warmups included? those change perf a lot on chat workloads

alex_chang: pasted logs below from the autoselector run (sm86):

```
# autoselector run summary
seqlen=480 -> selected kernel: quant_int4_tiled_v2 (expected latency 6.8ms)
seqlen=512 -> selected kernel: quant_int4_longseq_v1 (expected latency 7.9ms)
fallback_policy: none
estimated_throughput_ratio: 1.05
observed p50: 8.3ms (actual)
```

alex_chang: note the selected kernel switches at 512 and the kernel's memory layout plus an extra matmul kernel causes the jump

jing_wu: last week perf-bot flagged something similar — looks like the autotuner's cost function underweights KV-cache miss penalty. When the cached KV is cold, int4 longseq path does extra memcpy and quant-dequant steps

perf-bot: [alert] autotune: sm86-int4_longseq_v1 shows 11% p50 regression vs baseline (int8_shortseq) for seqlen in [496..528]

maria_liu: proposed quick mitigations:
- add hysteresis: require stable improvement over 3 minibatches before switching kernel
- add kv_cache_penalty term to cost fn (weight 0.2 by default)
- sequence_length_buckets: prefer int8 for seqlen >= 500 on sm86/sm83 unless throughput gain > 1.2x

samir: +1 to hysteresis. also we should prefer kernels that avoid extra copies when kv_cache.hot=false. We can detect hot/cold from cache hit ratio in the first 5 tokens and bump penalty

ron_smith: i repro'd locally on an nv-1 with sm86. Microbench script: `python perf/run_infer.py --model gpt-small --quant int4 --seq 512 --batch 1 --profile nsight` produced a 9% p50 increase vs int8. nvprof traces show extra `cudaMemcpy` at kernel boundary

alex_chang: thinking of a config patch for autotuner defaults. draft snippet: 
```
{"autotune": {
  "hysteresis_windows": 3,
  "kv_cache_penalty": 0.2,
  "seqlen_bucket_policy": [
    {"min": 0, "max": 256, "prefer": "int4"},
    {"min": 257, "max": 499, "prefer": "int4"},
    {"min": 500, "max": 4096, "prefer": "int8", "min_throughput_win": 1.2}
  ],
  "arch_overrides": {
    "sm90": {"allow_fp8": true, "int4_penalty": 0.05},
    "sm86": {"int4_penalty": 0.25}
  }
}}
```

jing_wu: arch_overrides look right. sm90 hardware has better fp8 kernels — should default to fp8 when model supports it and seqlen > 1024. Also set `int4_penalty` per-arch so we avoid auto-select on older archs

maria_liu: testing plan:
1) add hysteresis + kv penalty to lab autotuner (canary on 2% of traffic)
2) collect p50/p95, kv_hit_ratio, kernel-switch counts over 24h
3) if p50 regression >3% on canary revert and iterate

samir: we should also tweak batching heuristics. current heuristic batches up to 8 if latency allows, but small batch window scheduling causes a kernel switch mid-window for mixed seqlen. Proposal: batch bucketing by seqlen bucket so kernels remain consistent per batch

alex_chang: yes — grouping by seqlen bucket reduced kernel churn in my local test and improved p50 by ~4% for mixed-chat traffic

ron_smith: i'll add a microbenchmark matrix across archs: sm83/sm86/sm90 x {int4,int8,fp8} x seqlen {64,256,480,512,1024} and dump raw nvtx markers. will post results by EOD

perf-bot: [info] scheduled job: microbench/quant-arch-matrix-1791004321 (ETA 6h)

maria_liu: one more thought — fallback hysteresis when capacity constrained: if we drop from int4->int8 due to autoscaler fallback, allow a delayed revert (cooldown 10s) to avoid flip-flopping under bursty load

alex_chang: agreed. thanks everyone — i'll push the config PR and tag @eng-runtime for review. keep an eye on perf-bot alerts after canary starts

samir: ping me on the PR, i want to validate the nsight traces and update the cost function math

jing_wu: +:thumbsup:
